originalTitle: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
summary: A lot of content on LinkedIn might seem like AI slop, and now, you'll be able to report those posts. As part of a series of updates to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform, LinkedIn is introducing an actual button that lets you flag a post as something that "Seems like AI […]
content: A lot of content on LinkedIn might seem like AI slop, and now, you’ll be able to report those posts. As part of a series of updates to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform, LinkedIn is introducing an actual button that lets you flag a post as something that “Seems like AI slop.” The new feature is part of a broader push to reduce the volume of apparent AI slop on the platform. AI detector Pangram recently found that 41 percent of longform LinkedIn posts were flagged as being completely generated by AI, as reported by 404Media. “AI slop is a top priority for all of us,” chief product officer Hari Srinivasan says in a post. “We really care about this.” In addition to the button to report a post as seemingly being AI-generated, LinkedIn is also ramping up new classifiers to identify “if a post is AI-slop or generally low-quality content,” which will “reduce the amount of AI slop you might see in suggested content and content from outside your network.” I’m currently seeing the new report button in the three-dots menu on posts. When I click it, LinkedIn hides the post and shows a message thanking me for my feedback. The new button will help LinkedIn “tune our models and make better feeds,” Srinivasan says. The company is also testing a way to show people that other users feel their posts come across as inauthentic or that they include heavy use of AI. In addition, LinkedIn is removing a feature that used AI to “enhance” a post and will replace it with a “feature that proofreads your words, but does not change your voice,” according to Srinivasan.

chineseContent: LinkedIn 上的很多内容可能看起来像是人工智能的废话，现在，你将能够举报这些帖子。作为减少平台上人工智能溢出量的一系列更新的一部分，LinkedIn 引入了一个实际按钮，可以让你将帖子标记为“看起来像人工智能溢出”。这项新功能是减少平台上明显的人工智能溢出量的更广泛努力的一部分。据 404Media 报道，人工智能检测器 Pangram 最近发现，41% 的长篇 LinkedIn 帖子被标记为完全由人工智能生成。 “人工智能问题是我们所有人的首要任务，”首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 在一篇文章中表示。 “我们真的很关心这个。”除了报告看似由 AI 生成的帖子的按钮外，LinkedIn 还推出了新的分类器，以识别“帖子是否为 AI 垃圾内容或普遍低质量的内容”，这将“减少您在建议内容和来自网络外部的内容中可能看到的 AI 垃圾数量”。我目前在帖子的三点菜单中看到了新的报告按钮。当我点击它时，LinkedIn 会隐藏该帖子并显示一条消息，感谢我的反馈。斯里尼瓦桑表示，新按钮将帮助 LinkedIn“调整我们的模型并提供更好的信息流”。该公司还在测试一种方法，向人们展示其他用户认为他们的帖子不真实，或者他们大量使用人工智能。此外，斯里尼瓦桑表示，LinkedIn 正在删除一项使用人工智能“增强”帖子的功能，并将其替换为“校对你的文字但不会改变你的声音的功能”。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
